transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah… I came in because my head just, I don’t know, it doesn’t seem to stay on task anymore. Like at work, I’ll be doing inventory for cleaning supplies, and I’ll look at the list and then somehow I’m just staring at it, not really taking it in. Or I’ll walk to the supply closet for something specific and by the time I get there I’m standing there like, “What did I come in here for?”

And I’ve been trying to study for a supervisor certification too, because I figured that might help me move up a little, but I keep reading the same line over and over. It’s like the words are there, but they don’t stick. I’ll realize I’ve been on the same paragraph for ten minutes and couldn’t tell you what it said. It’s frustrating, and kind of embarrassing, honestly, because I’m not trying to slack off. I just can’t keep my mind where it’s supposed to be.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yeah… most days, honestly. It’s not always like I’m crying or anything dramatic like that, but it’s this heavy, flat feeling that kind of follows me around. Like I’ll be at work just pushing the cleaning cart down an empty hallway, and everything feels… dull, I guess. Heavy. Like I’m moving through the day but not really in it.

And even when I’m home with my family, I’m trying to act normal, trying to sit there and be part of things, but inside it’s still there. I don’t know how to explain it exactly—just down, kind of weighed down, most of the time.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?

I don’t know… anxious, maybe not exactly? I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m walking around panicking or feeling like something terrible is about to happen all the time. It’s more like I’m tense in the background sometimes, if that makes sense, but I’m not sure if that’s anxiety or just being tired of feeling the way I’ve been feeling.

Like, I can get irritated or kind of wound up when I’m trying to get through the day and things aren’t clicking, but I don’t know that I’d call it being on edge. I guess I haven’t really thought of it that way. Mostly I notice the heaviness more than nervousness.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I haven’t really sat down and thought, like, “Do I enjoy this less than before?” It’s kind of hard for me to separate enjoying something from just going through my normal routine, if that makes sense.

Like, some things I’ll still do because that’s what I normally do, but I don’t know if I’d say I’ve been paying attention to whether I’m enjoying them or not. I guess I’d have to think about it more. What do you mean exactly—like hobbies, or time with people, or just anything that used to feel good?
Are there things you used to look forward to that you no longer look forward to?

I’m… not sure. I know that sounds like I’m dodging the question, but I really don’t know if I’ve been tracking it that clearly.

There are things I do, or things that are part of my normal life, and I guess I used to maybe anticipate them more, but I don’t know if I can say for sure that I “no longer look forward” to them. It’s more like the days kind of run together, and I’m just thinking about getting through what’s in front of me. Work, home, the usual stuff. So if there’s something coming up, I don’t always have that feeling of, “Oh, that’ll be nice,” but I also don’t know if that means I’ve stopped looking forward to it or if I’m just not paying much attention to that feeling.

Like when people ask things that way, I start trying to compare now to before, and then I get stuck because I can’t tell what’s changed exactly. I can say I haven’t really noticed myself getting excited about much, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing you’re asking.
Do you feel like you've been taking pleasure in things as much as you used to?

I’m honestly not sure. I know that probably sounds like the same answer again, but it’s hard for me to measure “pleasure,” you know? Like, I can do something and not hate it, but whether I’m getting as much out of it as I used to… I don’t know.

I guess I don’t really stop and think, “Am I enjoying this right now?” Most of the time I’m just doing what I normally do, getting through the day, and then later if someone asks me if it felt good or fun, I kind of draw a blank. It’s not like I can point to one thing and say, “I used to love that and now I feel nothing.” It’s more unclear than that.

Maybe I’ve been less aware of pleasure, if that makes sense, but I don’t know if that means it’s actually less or I’m just not paying attention to it. What do you mean by pleasure—like actually feeling happy in the moment, or just being able to enjoy something at all?
Have you noticed any decrease in the pleasure you get from activities that you normally enjoy?

I guess… I haven’t really noticed it in a clear way. Like I don’t have a specific activity in my head where I can say, “Yeah, I used to get a lot of pleasure from that and now I don’t.” It’s more that I’m not always paying attention to whether I’m enjoying something while I’m doing it.

I’ll do the things I normally do, and maybe they’re fine, maybe they’re just part of the routine, but I don’t usually stop and check, “Was that pleasurable?” So if you’re asking whether I’ve noticed a decrease, I’d probably say I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed it enough to describe it confidently.

I can say I don’t feel especially excited about much, but I also don’t know if that’s the same as a decrease in pleasure. It’s kind of hard for me to tell the difference between not enjoying something and just being on autopilot.
Can you think of anything recently that you've done and actually felt happy about?

I’m trying to think of something specific, and I’m kind of coming up blank, honestly. Not in the sense that nothing at all has been okay, but “actually felt happy about” feels like a pretty strong way to put it.

Like, I can get through something and think, “Okay, that’s done,” or “That wasn’t bad,” but I don’t know if I’d call that happy. Sometimes there might be a small moment where something feels a little lighter, maybe, but it doesn’t really stand out enough for me to point to it and say, “Yes, that made me happy.”

I guess if you asked me what I did recently, I could list normal things, but if the question is whether I clearly felt happy while doing them… I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed that feeling in a way I can grab onto.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?

I don’t really know. I mean, I haven’t been tracking it or anything, so I don’t want to say yes or no too confidently. My clothes seem more or less the same, I think, but I also don’t weigh myself regularly, so unless it was a big change I might not notice.

Sometimes I’ll look in the mirror and wonder if I look different, but then I can’t tell if that’s real or just me being in my head about it. So… no clear change that I’ve noticed, I guess.
Have you lost or gained a significant amount of weight recently?

No, not that I can clearly say. I mean, “significant” makes me think like something obvious, like my clothes suddenly not fitting or people commenting on it, and that hasn’t really happened.

I haven’t been stepping on a scale or keeping track, so I guess it’s possible there’s been some small change that I just haven’t noticed. But as far as I can tell, nothing major. My pants and work clothes seem about the same, and I haven’t had that feeling of, like, “Oh, I’ve really gained weight,” or “I’ve really dropped weight.” So I’d say no significant change that I know of.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I feel tired a lot, but “more than usual” is hard for me to judge because I don’t really have a clear baseline in my head anymore.

Some days I’ll think, “Yeah, I’m worn out,” but then I also think, well, maybe that’s just because work is work, and I’m on my feet, and everybody gets tired. I haven’t noticed some sudden big change where I’m like, “Wow, I can’t function because I’m so much more tired than before.” It’s more… I don’t know, kind of blended into the background.

So I guess I’d say I’m tired, but I don’t know if it’s more than usual in a way I can clearly point to.
Can you remember the last time you felt genuinely interested or excited about something?

I’m not sure I can remember one clearly, honestly. Like, I know there must have been moments where I was at least interested in something, because I still do things, I still watch stuff or talk to people sometimes, but “genuinely excited” feels like a harder bar.

I keep trying to think of an example, and my mind kind of goes blank. Not in a dramatic way, just… I don’t know, nothing is jumping out at me. Maybe there are little moments where I think, “Oh, that sounds okay,” or I get curious about something for a few minutes, but I don’t know if I’d call that excited.

So I guess the honest answer is I can’t really remember the last time in a specific way. It’s not like I have a date or an event I can point to and say, “Yeah, that was it.”
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that would normally bring you happiness?

I don’t know if I’d say I’m completely unable to feel pleasure. That sounds very definite, like nothing ever feels good at all, and I’m not sure that’s exactly it.

It’s more like… things don’t really hit the way I think they’re supposed to. Like if I do something that should be enjoyable, I might still recognize, “Okay, this is a decent thing,” or “This is better than sitting around doing nothing,” but I don’t get that strong feeling of happiness from it. Or at least not in a way that feels very clear to me.

I guess part of the problem is I’m not always sure what “normal” is supposed to feel like anymore. So when you ask if I’m unable to experience pleasure, I kind of want to say maybe, or partly, but then I second-guess it because it’s not like I never feel anything positive. It’s just muted, I guess. Like the volume is turned down.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

I don’t know… guilty, maybe not in a specific way. Like, I’m trying to think if there’s something lately where I’ve done something wrong and I’m carrying it around, and nothing really clear comes to mind.

I mean, I can second-guess myself about things, like whether I handled a conversation right or whether I’m doing enough in general, but I don’t know if I’d call that guilt exactly. It’s more like this vague uncomfortable feeling sometimes, but not tied to one thing where I could say, “Yes, I feel guilty about that.”

So I guess my answer is… not really, or at least not that I’ve noticed clearly.
Do you feel like things you used to enjoy are now empty or unfulfilling?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, “empty” sounds pretty strong, but… yeah, maybe sometimes. It’s hard for me to tell if the things themselves feel empty or if I’m just not bringing much to them, if that makes sense.

Like, I can still do things I used to enjoy, or at least things I used to think of as relaxing or pleasant, and I’ll get through them. I might even think, “This is fine,” but afterward it doesn’t really leave much behind. It’s not like I feel refreshed or satisfied exactly. It’s more like I did the activity, and then it’s over, and I’m kind of the same as before.

But I don’t want to overstate it either. I wouldn’t say every single thing feels completely pointless or anything. It’s just… a lot of things don’t feel as rewarding as I imagine they should. I notice myself doing them more out of habit than because I’m really looking forward to them. So maybe unfulfilling is a fair word, but I’d say it’s more muted or flat than totally empty.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to find enjoyable?

I’m not sure I’d put it as a total loss of interest. It’s more complicated than that, I guess. I still do some of the same things, and if someone asked me whether I “like” them, I’d probably still say yes, because in my head I remember liking them. But when it comes time to actually do them, there isn’t always much pull toward them.

Like, I don’t always feel that feeling of wanting to go do something because it sounds enjoyable. It’s more like, “Well, I could do that,” or “That’s something I usually do,” and then I either do it kind of automatically or I put it off. And I don’t know if that counts as losing interest or if it’s more that the interest is still there in theory but not very strong in practice.

I guess I’m hesitant to say yes outright because it makes it sound like I’ve stopped caring about everything I used to enjoy, and that’s not exactly true. But compared to how I imagine it used to feel, or how other people seem to talk about enjoying things, yeah, the interest feels kind of dulled. Not gone, just harder to access.
Have you noticed any significant change in your appetite lately?

I don’t think so, not in a way that I’ve really noticed. My appetite is one of those things I don’t pay a ton of attention to unless it’s really obvious, like if I’m suddenly not eating at all or I’m constantly hungry, and I wouldn’t say either of those is happening.

I mean, some days I might eat kind of normally, and other days it’s more just whatever is convenient, but that feels pretty typical for me. I haven’t had that thing where food seems disgusting or where I’m losing my appetite across the board. And I also haven’t noticed myself eating a lot more than usual, at least not enough that I’d call it a significant change.

So… no, I guess I’d say nothing significant with appetite, or nothing I can clearly point to.
Have you had anyone comment on your weight changing recently?

Not really, no. At least nobody’s said anything to me directly like, “Hey, you’ve lost weight,” or “You look heavier,” or anything like that.

I guess it’s possible there are small changes I wouldn’t notice, or people might notice and just not say anything, but I haven’t had anyone comment on it. My clothes don’t feel dramatically different either, not that I’ve been checking carefully. So I’d say no, no one’s really mentioned my weight changing recently.
Have you lost a noticeable amount of weight recently?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t been weighing myself regularly, so I can’t give you an exact number or anything, but nothing has stood out to me as a noticeable loss.

Like I said, my clothes seem to fit about the same, at least as far as I can tell, and nobody’s pointed anything out. If there’s been a few pounds one way or the other, I probably wouldn’t notice, honestly. But a noticeable amount? No, I wouldn’t say that.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight unintentionally?

No, not that I’m aware of. I mean, the “unintentionally” part is kind of hard because I haven’t been trying to lose weight, but I also haven’t noticed any significant drop either.

I don’t really track my weight closely. I’m not stepping on a scale every week or anything like that, so I can’t say, “Oh, I lost exactly this many pounds.” But just going by how my clothes fit and what I see in the mirror, nothing seems really different. Nobody’s brought it up to me either.

So I’d say no, I haven’t lost a significant amount of weight unintentionally, at least not that I’ve noticed.

doctor.question: Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to find enjoyable?

I’m not sure I’d put it as a total loss of interest. It’s more complicated than that, I guess. But when it comes time to actually do them, there isn’t always much pull toward them.

Like, I don’t always feel that feeling of wanting to go do something because it sounds enjoyable. It’s more like, “Well, I could do that,” or “That’s something I usually do,” and then I either do it kind of automatically or I put it off. And I don’t know if that counts as losing interest or if it’s more that the interest is still there in theory but not very strong in practice.

I guess I’m hesitant to say yes outright because it makes it sound like I’ve stopped caring about everything I used to enjoy, and that’s not exactly true. But compared to how I imagine it used to feel, or how other people seem to talk about enjoying things, yeah, the interest feels kind of dulled. Not gone, just harder to access.
